claims.title: Why do the invariant periods form an invertible matrix?
claims.hypotheses: K is a finite extension of the ℓ-adic field. Fix compatible semistable period rings and a rational semistable representation of rank d with a chosen basis.
claims.statement: There is a square invertible polynomial period matrix whose columns are invariant tensors.

claims.title: Why do the derivatives of the period columns give a nilpotent matrix?
claims.hypotheses: Use the invariant polynomial period basis, the Galois action on its variable and the crystalline non-coboundary for the original Kummer cocycle.
claims.statement: The right logarithmic derivative and the Frobenius comparison have entries in the unramified coefficient field. The derivative is nilpotent of exponent at most d.

claims.title: How do Galois and Frobenius act at logarithm zero?
claims.hypotheses: Fix the normalized logarithm L=X+b, whose Frobenius is ℓL and whose Galois displacement is c(g)t. Evaluate the invertible invariant matrix at X=−b.
claims.statement: Galois acts on its specialization by a right finite exponential with the signed monodromy. The two Frobenius comparators and the monodromy admit integral Witt multiples.

claims.title: Which denominator makes every coefficient of the Galois correction integral?
claims.hypotheses: The normalized monodromy matrix has dth power zero. The displacement c(g) is integral and vanishes on the subgroup fixing the chosen roots.
claims.statement: One common factorial exponent clears the finite exponential for every g; on the fixing subgroup the cleared matrix is the scalar ℓ^k₀ times the identity.

claims.title: How does a scalar approximation correct all the columns at once?
claims.hypotheses: For each filtration depth a scalar power-series witness divisible by E approximates the logarithmic displacement for every g.
claims.statement: A single cleared polynomial matrix at that depth corrects the action up to the prescribed filtration step and reduces to a scalar modulo E.

claims.statement: There are integral lifts with two filtration bounds, and their images define normalized starting matrices and the Galois correction on the coefficient disc.

claims.statement: Above the threshold for the rational period pair, one can choose a common height and two integral matrices whose product is a scalar and whose ordered products have the required filtration.
